answer: Each agent commits a 64 GB RAM array and the verifier issues meadow probes demanding nanosecond memory-bus latency readings at random offsets. The agent must answer within a 40 ms budget, proving the array sits in local DRAM and is not paged or shared. One honest agent holds one 64 GB array costing about $180, while 10 fakes must hold 640 GB and answer 10 parallel probe streams. The verifier replays a sample of zephyr readings and slashes the bond of any agent over budget, freezing repeat pigment offenders from the next epoch.
